title: How a Star Can Leave a Black Hole — 60 Second Test

scenes.narration: Deep inside a massive star, gravity pulls everything inward. Energy from fusion pushes outward, helping the star hold its shape.
When the core can no longer make enough outward pressure, gravity takes over. The core contracts rapidly, while outer layers react.
Some massive stars leave black holes behind. The event horizon is a boundary: once light crosses inward, it cannot escape.
Outside that boundary, light travels through curved spacetime. The path can bend visibly, changing what distant observers see behind the black hole.
Gravity pulls more strongly at closer distances. Across an object, that difference creates tidal forces, which can stretch it toward the black hole.
Black holes vary enormously in mass. Some are stellar remnants; the largest known examples contain millions or billions of Suns.
